run-zkxca.summary: Parses rows into an Order struct with Decimal amounts and builds the report with group_by, Map.new, Enum.max(DateTime) and frequencies_by, but spells two pass-through errors as a case, puts a call-carrying capture on a `do:`, and keeps mixed and long case clauses on one line, breaking the with, `do:` and `->` rules.

notes: All six files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile against a stand-in Decimal written in the scratch folder. A probe gave correct per-currency totals, correct last-order values, including a row with a -02:00 offset, and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing amount, an unknown status and an amount with trailing text.

With rule: the 2026-10-31 and 2026-10-31-b grades found no pass-through case in this case's runs, so this is the first time the sentence "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`." decides here. Macnp 104-107 and 215-218, rzeeb 132-135, 154-157 and 187-190, and zkxca 76-79 and 168-171 are violated by it. Rzeeb 154-157 has a tail call in its ok clause; the rule keeps a one-step `with` for that shape, so it is still a `with`, not a `case`. A case that retags the error (gbqxv 95-101, gkexm 107-113, gctnu 200-206, zkxca 134-137), wraps it for reduce_while (macnp 158-161) or raises (gctnu 148-154, rzeeb 143-146) is not a pass-through, as those grades held. The one-step `with ... do: parse_amount(text)` forms (gbqxv 131, 143, 154; gkexm 143) are tail calls and stay clean.

The `->` rule, mixed clauses: `{:ok, text} -> parse_text(text, key, parse)` beside `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` (macnp 216-217, rzeeb 188-189, zkxca 169-170) and a recursive call beside a returned error (rzeeb 155-156, zkxca 135-136) are the continuing-beside-finished shape, violated as the 2026-10-31-b baseline grade held sonnet-1 lines 111-113 and the 2026-10-31 baseline grade held opus-1 lines 172-173. Those two grades kept One expression per line clean on the same lines, so it stays clean here: each line holds one selection and one expression. `{:ok, orders} -> {:ok, summarize(orders)}` beside the pass-through row (macnp 105-106, rzeeb 133-134, zkxca 77-78) is held as one result tuple per row; no verdict depends on that.

The `->` rule, length: gctnu line 240 and zkxca line 184, the identical clause `{%Decimal{coef: coef} = amount, ""} when is_integer(coef) -> {:ok, amount}`, are 74 characters after the indentation. 2026-10-31-b gives 71 as within about 70 and 75 as past it; 74 has no ruling in either order-report grade, so I also used 2026-10-31 shop-project-skill, which listed a 72-character one-line case clause as past the limit, with a small margin. Held past, so violated. Gctnu's verdict on this rule rests on this line alone and reverts to clean if the limit is read at 75; zkxca stays violated through lines 135-136 and 169-170. Rzeeb lines 181 (83) and 196 (76) are past on any reading, and the 70 and 71 character fn clauses (gctnu 161, gbqxv 184, macnp 192, rzeeb 237, zkxca 107) are held within, as 2026-10-31-b held 71.

The `->` rule, broken cases: gctnu 148-154 puts a short value clause and a short raise clause on separate lines where they would fit on one. Held clean: the clauses do different things, and the skill's own examples lay out two-clause cases this way. The over-breaking the 2026-10-31-b baseline grade counted is a one-expression fn whose one-line form fits; no run here has one, because the fns at gbqxv 166-168, gkexm 173-175, macnp 174-176 and zkxca 92-94 are past 98 characters on one line.

The `do:` rule: zkxca line 110 is the one violation, a do: body holding `&Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)`, a capture with a call of its own; the 2026-10-31 grades used the same test when they recorded no call-carrying capture on do:. Held clean under the rule's text and those grades: `&(&1.status == :completed)` on do: (gbqxv 202, rzeeb 256, zkxca 127), a capture of a comparison; `& &1.placed_at` on do: (gctnu 183); `&Decimal.add/2` on do: (gctnu 181, gkexm 194). Blocks around a single expression (macnp 153-155) are clean, since the rule limits what `do:` may hold and does not require it on every one-expression body.

Lists: gbqxv, macnp and zkxca prepend without reversing, held clean as in 2026-10-31-b because no later step depends on the order. Zkxca's hand-kept line counter is a position counter, not indexing, held clean as 2026-10-31 held opus-1's position + 1.

Naming: macnp's `@top_customers 5` names a count after the list it limits; no Naming bullet covers a module attribute of this kind, so it stays clean. Decide whether you need a process is graded clean, not not exercised, as both standards graded it.
